Uplink IT Academy

A training environment for the transition from help-desk support to network engineering. It combines certification item banks, a simulated service desk and command-line laboratories, and each laboratory is checked automatically before it is published.

Visit the site ↗How to useIn motion

01

Problem statement

Certification preparation relies mostly on question banks and slide decks, which measure recall rather than procedure. Many candidates pass the examination without ever having isolated a fault with a terminal, a directory service or a remote session, so the competence the credential implies is first observed during a production incident.

02

Contribution

Three instruments are arranged in sequence. Item banks of 200 original scenario questions per set, each with an explanation and a reference, address declarative knowledge. A service-desk simulation for a fictional company, Harborline Logistics, with a ticket queue, directory, server room, remote desktop, mail console and asset register, addresses diagnosis in context. Command-line laboratories for Windows, Linux, security and Cisco IOS address procedure: each objective is checked as the learner types. A troubleshooting coach, short courses, a career agent that reads a résumé, and Network Docs, a documentation service for businesses, complete the environment.

03

Architecture

A React and TypeScript client on a Postgres back end, with Stripe for per-item purchases. Progress, experience points and streaks are attached to an account, while samples remain open without authentication so that every module can be evaluated before purchase.

04

Method and data

Each laboratory is a declarative record: a simulated device, a scripted shell and an ordered list of checks. Because the learner and the grader use the same execution engine, the reference solution can be replayed against the checks before release, and a laboratory whose solution fails is withheld. A scheduled job produces one candidate laboratory per track every day and publishes only those that pass the replay.

05

Verification and limitations

Verification is part of the content pipeline rather than a later review: no laboratory reaches learners without a passing reference run. The shells simulate Windows, Linux and IOS behaviour and are not virtual machines, so commands outside the modelled set are not interpreted. The questions are original and are not official examination items.
